## Context / Problem

The 2026-08-05/06 rebar-janitor run surfaced three gaps in the packaged skill at
`examples/agent-skills/rebar-janitor/`:

1. Discovery's concern list stopped at eight and had no concern covering **unwired /
   partially wired functionality** — values accepted at a surface and then silently
   dropped — which was the highest-yield class of finding in that run.
2. Two concerns (comment quality, test-suite health) are too large for a single
   subagent, and the skill gave no sharding or streaming-validation guidance, so a run
   either batched an unreviewable pool at the end or skipped the concern on volume
   grounds.
3. Verification had no guidance for validating a sharded discovery stream.

The findings are already written up in the working tree of the operator's main
checkout (the live skill is a symlink into this repo, so edits land there first). This
ticket lands that exact content on `main` through Gerrit; it does not re-derive or
re-author it.

## Approach

Documentation-only edit of three Markdown files in the packaged example skill. The
content is fixed and already authored — this ticket copies it verbatim into a fresh
worktree branched from `origin/main`, verifies byte-identity against the source with
`diff`, and lands it as one Gerrit change. No Python source, no tests, no runtime
behavior changes; the skill is prose consumed by an agent harness, so prose is the
deliverable and verbatim transfer (not re-authoring) is what keeps the landed text
identical to the text the janitor run actually produced.

Concretely, the three edits are:

- **`phases/discovery.md`** — add concerns 9, 10, 11 after concern 8, and change
  "eight concerns" to "eleven concerns" in the output schema:
  - **(9) Unwired & partially wired functionality** — values accepted then silently
    dropped (a parameter never read; a CLI flag parsed but unconsumed; a request field
    the callee omits; a kwarg after `**kwargs`; a protocol with no implementers). Use a
    linter unused-argument rule (Ruff `ARG*`) in a scratch config **for detection only**;
    resolve the full surface-to-consumer path (reaching a struct is not "wired" unless
    the struct is read); cross-check docs, `--help` text, MCP tool descriptions and ADRs
    for false promises; rank honestly-documented dead surfaces last rather than dropping
    them.
  - **(10) Comment quality & rationale placement** — a taxonomy routing history to the
    ticket system, architecture to ADRs, logic to the code, and data shapes to schema;
    measure comment share and comment-growth-vs-code-growth rate; shard by subsystem
    with a directory scope and line budget; and require each shard's `do_not_move` list
    to be appended to the playbook **before** any edit lands.
  - **(11) Test-suite health** — wasteful duplication, change-detector tests, whether
    the implied regression confidence is earned, and optimizations that cut maintenance
    or wall-clock without cutting behavioral / contractual / integration / regression
    coverage; check whether any size/duplication/skip gate exists; shard by test-tree
    region.
- **`phases/verification.md`** — a new "Streaming validation (use when Discovery is
  sharded)" section: verify each shard as it arrives rather than batching, validate
  along three axes at once (correctness, impact validity, remediation-direction
  validity), and keep blindness unrelaxed.
- **`SKILL.md`** — two operating principles: shard the two oversized concerns and stream
  their validation; and "volume is not a reason to skip a concern."

## Scope

Three files, all under the packaged example skill (all already exist):

- `examples/agent-skills/rebar-janitor/SKILL.md` — +6/-1
- `examples/agent-skills/rebar-janitor/phases/discovery.md` — +63/-1
- `examples/agent-skills/rebar-janitor/phases/verification.md` — +13/-0

No files outside `examples/agent-skills/rebar-janitor/` change. No `src/rebar` file
changes, so no test file changes are implied.

## Testing

No new testable behavior is added: these files are prose read by an agent harness, not
code that any test imports or executes. Verification is therefore transfer-fidelity plus
the repo's existing gates:

- `diff` of each worktree file against the operator checkout's working-tree version
  exits 0 (byte-identical transfer, no re-authoring).
- `make lint` and `make typecheck` pass (run by the pre-commit hook on commit).
- CI's `Verified` label on the Gerrit change is `+1`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `examples/agent-skills/rebar-janitor/phases/discovery.md` contains numbered
      concerns `9.`, `10.` and `11.` immediately after concern 8 and before the
      "### Temporal decay pass" heading; checked with
      `grep -n '^9\. \*\*Unwired' examples/agent-skills/rebar-janitor/phases/discovery.md`
      exiting 0 (and likewise for `10. **Comment quality` and `11. **Test-suite health`).
- [x] The output-schema line in that file reads "which of the eleven concerns above";
      checked by `grep -c 'eight concerns' …/discovery.md` returning 0 and
      `grep -c 'eleven concerns' …/discovery.md` returning 1.
- [x] `examples/agent-skills/rebar-janitor/phases/verification.md` contains an H2
      `## Streaming validation (use when Discovery is sharded)` that precedes the
      existing `## Verifier discipline` H2; checked by `grep -n '^## '` showing that
      order.
- [x] `examples/agent-skills/rebar-janitor/SKILL.md` states both new operating
      principles; checked by `grep -c 'Volume is not a reason to skip a concern'`
      returning 1 and the "One concern per subagent" bullet mentioning
      `Streaming validation`.
- [x] Each of the three landed files is byte-identical to the corresponding
      working-tree file in the operator's main checkout; checked by `diff` on all three
      pairs exiting 0 before the commit is created.
- [x] `make lint` and `make typecheck` exit 0 in the worktree (enforced by the
      pre-commit hook, so a created commit is itself the evidence).
- [x] The change carrying these three files reaches `Verified +1` and `LLM-Review +1`
      on Gerrit and is submitted to `main`; checked by
      `git log origin/main --oneline -- examples/agent-skills/rebar-janitor/` showing the
      commit after `git fetch origin`.
